passage:
Wednesday. Finished the report at five thirty. Kavitha Ma'am and the seniors were still at their desks, so I opened old emails and pretended to work until eight. Nobody asked me to stay. I just couldn't be the first one out and look lazy. The bus was full and the dinner was cold when I got home.
Lying here I keep thinking: what does Ma'am actually see? A chair filled after hours. She hasn't even opened my report.
Tomorrow I will send the report at five thirty, with a two-line summary, and ask if she needs anything else before I go. If that feels wrong, I will ask her what she prefers. Better to be judged on the work than on the chair.
Yogesh

qa.q: What time did Yogesh finish the report?
qa.a: Yogesh finished the report at five thirty.

qa.q: What was Yogesh feeling while staying at the desk until eight?
qa.a: Yogesh felt anxious about looking lazy and pressured to copy the seniors, even though the work was done.

qa.q: What plan does Yogesh make for the next day?
qa.a: Yogesh will send the report at five thirty with a short summary and ask Ma'am if anything else is needed before leaving, so results speak louder than presence.

qa.q: What might Kavitha Ma'am actually be noticing about the late-staying juniors?
qa.a: She may notice a filled chair, as Yogesh guesses, but she has not opened the report, so she may be judging the work less than the presence.

grounding: A new hire stays after hours to look committed though the work is done, then plans to show results and set honest limits.

Vasudha: Ok. Going home now 🙂
